        ### Question
        A 26-year-old woman comes to the physician because she has not had a menstrual period for 5 weeks. Menarche was at the age of 14 years and menses occurred at regular 30-day intervals. She reports having unprotected sexual intercourse 3 weeks ago. A urine pregnancy test is positive. Which of the following best describes the stage of development of the embryo at this time?

        ### Options
        opa. Sexual differentiation has begun, but fetal movement has not started
opb. Fetal heart is beating, but cardiac activity is not yet visible on ultrasound
opc. Limb buds have formed, but fetal movements have not begun
opd. Neural crest has formed, but limb buds have not yet formed
ope. Implantation has occured, but notochord has not yet formed

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Positive urine pregnancy test" -> "Implantation has occurred" -> "Embryo is in early development stage" -> "Limb buds have formed, but fetal movements have not begun" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Positive urine pregnancy test" -> "Implantation has occurred" -> "Embryo is developing" -> "Neural crest has formed" -> "Limb buds have not yet formed" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Positive urine pregnancy test" -> "Implantation has occurred" -> "Embryo is in the 5-6 week range" -> "Fetal heart is beating" -> "Cardiac activity may not be visible on ultrasound" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Positive urine pregnancy test" -> "Implantation has occurred" -> "Embryo is in early gestational age" -> "Sexual differentiation has begun" -> "Fetal movement has not started" -> 70%

### Retrieved Evidence Paths (broad but correct):
